results.caption:
Indians have become so unhealthy that we are literally failing at the 4 biggest benchmarks to measure health globally... 

Let’s look at all 4, and also see the hidden reasons why this is happening... it’s not just because of low protein intake...

1/ HALE or Healthy Life Expectancy, which is the age till which people are able to live a fully healthy life free of illness and support of others for care... 

where an average Indian has a HALE age of only 58... where US is 6 years ahead of us, China is almost 11 years ahead of us...

And we are almost 4 years behind the global average.

2/ Pre-diabetes - So the global benchmark for number of people with diabetes is about 12% of the population...

And when you look at India’s number currently, while about 12% people have diabetes, over 15% of the population is currently pre-diabetic, which means more than 1 in every 4 people have a blood sugar problem at the moment.

3/ Cardiovascular Health - where all problems culminate to bring things like strokes and heart attacks - and we have such a large population across all symptoms of the same like hyper-tension, abdominal fat...

The problem being that even if our number is at the global average, our population being much younger than that of other countries, Indians are getting it easily 10 years earlier than they should.

4/ Sarcopenia - loss of muscle mass and physical function - where measures like grip strength for Indians is lower than populations in US and China... and our muscle loss begins to happen at an earlier age

There are 3 big mistakes which Indians make...

1/ Ghee is healthy... While it may be better than other fats on certain benchmarks, but it has no protein, and the reason for a lot of these issues is protein deficiency...

2/ Walking is a great exercise... which builds absolutely no muscle... and unless we get people on to strength training, it will solve nothing no matter how much cardio, running and walking we do... 10k steps is in addition to weights, not instead of...

results.caption:
Hilarious way to lose a game 😭💀

In 2002, Cleveland led the Chiefs 39-37 with seconds remaining when Browns linebacker Dwayne Rudd thought he sacked Trent Green on the final play. Rudd immediately ripped off his helmet and threw it in celebration, thinking the game was over.

Green had actually lateraled the ball to offensive lineman John Tait before going down, and Tait continued running as the clock hit zero. Rudd was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct for removing his helmet, and because an NFL game cannot end on an accepted defensive penalty, Kansas City was awarded an untimed down. 

Morten Andersen then kicked a 30-yard field goal with 0:00 on the clock, giving the Chiefs a 40-39 win.

(@nfl @nfloncbs)
